0.long_answer: The cerebral cortex is the largest part of the brain responsible for neural integration in the central nervous system. It plays a crucial role in processing and integrating sensory, motor, and cognitive information. In the context of epilepsy, abnormal, excessive, or hypersynchronous neuronal activity in the cerebral cortex can lead to the generation of epileptic seizures. This malfunction in the cortical neural networks is a key factor in the pathophysiology of epilepsy.
